sources.provider: Soliman and Sergio; SEAFDEC/AQD institutional repository; Philippine lakes proceedings

reuse.metadata: Cite Soliman and Sergio and the official SEAFDEC/AQD repository record and PDF.

reuse.content: No item-specific license or permission verified. Retain only a short attributed research summary. The primary diet source Sergio (1995) is cited as an unpublished B.S. thesis and was not independently retrieved. No public-app reuse approval.

caveats: Although the 2001 paper title names Lake Buhi, it attributes the diet result to Sergio (1995) and explicitly places the diet study in Lake Manapao. Do not assign the percentages to Lake Buhi.
The diet sentence reports 92% zooplankton and describes other material as 8% phytoplankton and undetermined digested items; the split among the latter categories is ambiguous in the accessible text.
The 2001 paper does not state the original diet method, sample count or diet-specific dates. Its nearby eight-month duration applies to fecundity data, not necessarily to diet sampling.
The article's claim that Nile tilapia prey on sinarapan is supported there by citations to Aypa et al. (1995) and Gindelberger (1981); those underlying works were not independently reviewed.

The text is historical and does not establish current distribution, abundance, fishing permission, sanctuary boundary or present-day law. No species, diet, predation, safety, legal or public-app row was admitted.
